discovery: Plasma-based particle acceleration: the laser wakefield accelerator and its experimental realization

nominees.name: Chandrashekhar Joshi
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

nominees.name: Victor Malka
nominees.affiliation: Weizmann Institute of Science, Israel, and Laboratoire d'Optique Appliquée, France

motivation: In 1979 Tajima (with the late John Dawson) showed theoretically that an intense laser pulse in a plasma drives a wake whose electric fields exceed those of conventional accelerators by three orders of magnitude. Joshi's pioneering experiments with beat-wave and plasma-wake schemes demonstrated that such plasma waves can be excited in a controlled way and can accelerate particles, establishing the field experimentally. Malka and co-workers obtained the first quasi-monoenergetic, high-quality electron beams from laser wakefields in 2004, turning a concept into a practical tool. These fields now reach GeV energies over centimetres and drive compact X-ray sources. The work rests on nonlinear plasma wave theory and has opened a new route to high-energy physics, radiation sources and strong-field QED studies in the laboratory. It is a clear case of theoretical insight followed by decisive measurement.
